content: 1. A cross-sectional study conducted across six European countries investigated the relationship between exposure to aircraft and road traffic noise and the prevalence of heart disease and stroke. The findings were published in Environmental Health (2013). 2. Floud et al. (2013) explored the associations between heart disease, stroke, and exposure to aircraft and road traffic noise as part of the HYENA study. The results were presented at the 42nd International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2013) in Innsbruck, Austria. 3. Floud et al. (2011) examined the use of medication in relation to noise exposure from aircraft and road traffic in six European countries, as part of the HYENA study. The findings were published in Occupational and Environmental Medicine. 4. Foraster et al. (2012) analyzed the impact of transportation noise, particularly railway noise, on blood pressure in two European cohorts (REGICOR and SAPALDIA). The results were presented at the 41st International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2012) in New York, USA. 5. Foraster et al. (2011) conducted a cross-sectional study in Girona, Spain, to assess the association between road traffic noise and hypertension in a population-based sample as part of the REGICOR-AIR project. The findings were presented at the 10th International Congress on Noise as a Public Health Problem (ICBEN 2011) in London, UK. 6. Foraster et al. (2013) investigated the independent effects of traffic-related noise and air pollution on blood pressure, focusing on indoor noise levels and protective measures. The study was presented at INTER-NOISE 2013 in Innsbruck, Austria. 7. Foraster et al. (2014a) examined the long-term effects of traffic-related air pollution on blood pressure and hypertension in an adult cohort in Spain as part of the REGICOR study. The findings were published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 8. Foraster et al. (2014b) studied the relationship between high blood pressure and long-term exposure to indoor noise and air pollution from road traffic. The results were published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 9. Frei et al. (2014) evaluated the effects of nocturnal road traffic noise exposure and annoyance on both objective and subjective sleep quality. The study was published in the International Journal of Hygiene and Environmental Health. 10. Fuks et al. (2011) investigated the long-term effects of urban particulate air pollution and traffic noise on arterial blood pressure. The findings were published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 11. Gan et al. (2012) assessed the association between long-term exposure to community noise and traffic-related air pollution and coronary heart disease mortality. The study was published in the American Journal of Epidemiology. 12. Garcia et al. (2018) conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of a military hearing conservation program, with findings published in Military Medicine. 13. Gelderblom et al. (2014) compared the impact of civil versus military aircraft noise on noise annoyance. The results were presented at the 43rd International Congress on Noise Control Engineering (INTER-NOISE 2014) in Melbourne, Australia. 14. Gidlöf-Gunnarsson et al. (2012) examined railway noise annoyance and the influence of factors such as the number of trains, ground vibration, and building situational factors. The study was published in Noise & Health. 15. Gidlöf-Gunnarsson and Öhrström (2010) explored the potential of quiet courtyards to mitigate urban residents' responses to road traffic noise. The findings were published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 16. Gidlöf-Gunnarsson et al. (2010) implemented a full-scale intervention based on the quiet side concept in a residential area exposed to road traffic noise. The effects on perceived sound environment and general noise annoyance were presented at INTER-NOISE 2010 in Lisbon, Portugal. 17. Gidlöf-Gunnarsson et al. (2013) evaluated the health and well-being effects of noise reduction measures, such as traffic diversion and tunnel construction, following the opening of the Southern Link. The findings were presented at INTER-NOISE 2013 in Innsbruck, Austria. 18. Gilles and Van de Heyning (2014) assessed the effectiveness of a preventive campaign targeting noise-induced hearing damage in adolescents. The study was published in the International Journal of Pediatric Otorhinolaryngology. 19. Grazuleviciene et al. (2004) investigated the relationship between traffic noise emissions and myocardial infarction risk, with findings published in the Polish Journal of Environmental Studies. 20. Green et al. (1982) studied the effects of aircraft noise on the reading ability of school-age children, with results published in Archives of Environmental Health. 21. Griefahn et al. (2000) analyzed physiological, subjective, and behavioral responses to noise from rail and road traffic. The study was published in Noise & Health. 22. Griffiths and Raw (1987) examined community and individual responses to changes in traffic noise exposure, with findings published in Developments in Toxicology and Environmental Science. 23. Griffiths and Raw (1989) investigated adaptation to changes in traffic noise exposure, with results published in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. 24. Guski (1999) explored personal and social variables as co-determinants of noise annoyance, with findings published in Noise & Health. 25. Guski et al. (2017) conducted a systematic review on environmental noise and annoyance for the WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region. The study was published in the International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. 26. Guyatt et al. (2008) introduced the GRADE system for rating the quality of evidence and strength of recommendations, with findings published in BMJ. 27. Hänninen et al. (2014) assessed the environmental burden of disease in Europe by evaluating nine risk factors across six countries. The study was published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 28. Haines et al. (2001a) examined the effects of chronic aircraft noise exposure on child health in the West London Schools Study, with findings published in Psychological Medicine. 29. Haines et al. (2001b) investigated the impact of chronic aircraft noise exposure on stress responses, mental health, and cognitive performance in school children, with results published in Psychological Medicine. 30. Haines et al. (2001c) conducted a follow-up study on the effects of chronic aircraft noise exposure on child stress responses and cognition, with findings published in the International Journal of Epidemiology. 31. Halonen et al. (2012) analyzed the associations between nighttime traffic noise and sleep disturbances in the Finnish Public Sector Study, with results published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 32. Hansell et al. (2013) conducted a small-area study on the relationship between aircraft noise and cardiovascular disease near Heathrow Airport in London, with findings published in BMJ. 33. Heimann et al. (2007) provided a comprehensive guide for authorities and consultants on air pollution, traffic noise, and related health effects in the Alpine region. 34. Hense et al. (1989) investigated noise as a risk factor for cardiovascular disease in field studies, with findings published in Sozialund Präventivmedizin. 35. Herbold et al. (1989) studied the effects of road traffic noise on the prevalence of hypertension in men, with results published in Sozialund Präventivmedizin. 36. Hérroux and Verbeek (2018a) summarized systematic reviews and meta-analyses on environmental noise for the WHO guidelines. 37. Hérroux and Verbeek (2018b) outlined the methodology for systematic evidence reviews for the WHO Environmental Noise Guidelines for the European Region. 38. Hohmann (2015) assessed the harmfulness of impulse noise to hearing, with findings presented at the 10th European Conference on Noise Control (EURONOISE 2015) in Maastricht, Netherlands. 39. Hong et al. (2010) evaluated the effects of long-term exposure to railway and road traffic noise on subjective sleep disturbance, with findings published in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America. 40. Hong et al. (2006) assessed sleep disturbance caused by nighttime railway noise through a field survey, with results presented at INTER-NOISE 2006 in Honolulu, USA. 41. Houthuijs and van Wiechen (2006) monitored health and perceptions around Schiphol Airport in the Netherlands. 42. Huang et al. (2006) evaluated the PICO framework as a knowledge representation for clinical questions, with findings presented at the AMIA Annual Symposium. 43. Huss et al. (2010) investigated the relationship between aircraft noise, air pollution, and mortality from myocardial infarction, with findings published in Epidemiology. 44. Hygge et al. (2002) conducted a prospective study on the effects of aircraft noise on cognitive performance in school children, with results published in Psychological Science. 45. ISO (2013) provided guidelines for estimating noise-induced hearing loss in ISO 1999:2013. 46. ISO (2016) outlined the description, measurement, and assessment of environmental noise in ISO 1996-1:2016. 47. Ising and Ising (2002) studied the chronic increase in cortisol levels during the first half of the night caused by road traffic noise, with findings published in Noise & Health. 48. Janssen and Vos (2009) compared recent surveys on aircraft noise exposure-response relationships, with findings published by TNO. 49. Janssen et al. (2011) compared exposure-response relationships for wind turbine noise annoyance and other noise sources, with findings published in the Journal of the Acoustical Society of America. 50. Jarup et al. (2008) investigated the relationship between hypertension and noise exposure near airports as part of the HYENA study, with findings published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 51. Jarup et al. (2005) described the study design and noise exposure assessment for the HYENA study, with findings published in Environmental Health Perspectives. 52. Karpaty et al. (2002) discussed variability and vulnerability at the ecological level and its implications for understanding social determinants of health, with findings published in the American Journal of Public Health. 53. Kastka (1981) evaluated the effects of traffic-silencing measures on noise nuisance, with findings published in Zeitschrift für Lärmbekämpfung. 54. Kastka et al. (1995) studied the long-term effects of noise protection barriers on residents' annoyance responses, with findings published in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. 55. Klatte et al. (2014) examined the effects of chronic aircraft noise exposure on cognitive performance and quality of life in elementary school children as part of the NORAH study. 56. Knipschild et al. (1984) investigated the relationship between transportation noise, psychological issues, and hypertension in Amsterdam residents. 57. Knopper and Ollson (2011) reviewed the health effects of wind turbines, with findings published in Environmental Health. 58. Kotowski et al. (2011) evaluated the effectiveness of brochures in reducing the risk of noise-induced hearing loss in college students, with findings published in Noise & Health. 59. Kuwano et al. (2014) conducted a social survey on wind turbine noise in Japan, with findings published in the Noise Control Engineering Journal. 60. Lam and Au (2008) studied human annoyance responses to changes in noise exposure following the opening of a new railway extension in Hong Kong. 61. Lambert and Philipps-Bertin (2008) conducted a national survey in France on perceptions and attitudes toward transportation noise. 62. Langdon and Griffiths (1982) compared subjective effects of traffic noise exposure using different noise indices and response scales, with findings published in the Journal of Sound and Vibration. 63. Lekaviciute (2007) studied the influence of traffic noise in Kaunas city on myocardial infarction risk as part of a PhD thesis. 64. Lercher et al. (2007) analyzed the effects of noise from combined traffic sources on annoyance, focusing on interactions between rail and road noise.
